I am an old man here in Iringa, and I have farmed this land for many seasons. The soil here still gives a good harvest if the rains come well, so I plant my maize together with beans as I always do. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from the shop — the price is too high for a poor man like me — but I put the manure from my few animals on the plot before planting. My wife and my grown children help me in the field, and when weeding time comes heavy I call two or three neighbors to help for a few days in exchange for some pay and food.
